targets.action_item: Make scoring configuration explicit rather than assuming standard fantasy points: support fractional values, negative events, PPR toggles, and defensive-player features in projections and evaluation.

targets.the_leak: FantasyPros snapshots expert rankings at the start of Thursday Night Football and Sunday 1 p.m. games, locks Thursday players, and evaluates a pool built from both Expert Consensus Rankings and actual fantasy leaders. It assigns projected points from the historical production of each rank slot, computes an Accuracy Gap, converts weekly gaps to z-scores, and drops the worst week from Week 8 onward.
targets.action_item: For fair model benchmarking, freeze inputs at game-lock times, include both consensus-selected and surprise performers, map ranks to historical slot production, and normalize weekly errors before removing an outlier week.

targets.the_leak: Sportradar says its live-data operation uses 12,600 scouts across 35 data applications and feeds, covering more than 900,000 events in 32 sports. It emphasizes accuracy, speed, depth, security, and integrity, and says its venue data capture can be AI-powered and produce up-to-the-second data and odds.
targets.action_item: Prioritize low-latency event capture, broad market/event coverage, and quality controls; combine venue-level human/scout provenance with automated collection and track integrity as a data-quality dimension.

targets.the_leak: Sportradar's Probabilities API provides live and pre-match three-way win/lose/draw probabilities, features top US bookmakers, covers NFL and other sports, and offers probability breakdowns plus a live timeline for supported games. The documentation distinguishes event probabilities from seasonal and seasonal-outright probabilities.
targets.action_item: Use bookmaker-aware probability signals in both pre-match and live models, retain the full probability timeline rather than only the latest value, and separate event-level from season/outright probability features.

targets.the_leak: FantasyPros markets a single REST API spanning NFL rankings, projections, players, news, injuries and scoring; its injury data includes injury designations and practice-report status.
targets.action_item: Prioritize a unified NFL data layer that combines consensus rankings, projections, player metadata, news and practice/injury status, with predictable JSON and one key.

targets.the_leak: RotoWire exposes an NFL injury-report table organized around player, team, position, injury, status and estimated return, and provides a team filter.
targets.action_item: Match the competitor baseline with a filterable injury monitor, but differentiate with historical status changes, update timestamps and export/API access.

targets.the_leak: Action Network compares its model odds with consensus odds and displays scheduled/open lines, pro line, grade, edge, best odds, bet percentage and money percentage; it states a B grade or 3.5% edge threshold for projection-only bets.
targets.action_item: Build a transparent model-vs-market screen with opening/current lines, edge, grade and price-shopping, while clearly labeling premium-locked fields.

targets.the_leak: BetMGM explains the core NFL market vocabulary: spread, moneyline, over/under totals, parlays, props and teasers. It describes vig and gives worked examples for spread and American moneyline payouts.
targets.action_item: Add inline education beside NFL lines: explain favorite/underdog spread outcomes, vig, moneyline payout math, pushes and totals so users can interpret odds without leaving the product.

targets.the_leak: AWS describes NFL Coverage Responsibility as three linked ML models: targeted defender, matchup, and assignment identification. The models use X/Y coordinates, speed and acceleration recorded 10 times per second, probabilistic frame-by-frame outputs, scheme inputs, spatial-temporal deep learning, and random play truncation during training.
targets.action_item: Use this as a methodology benchmark: model defensive responsibility probabilistically at frame level, publish the tracking cadence/features and validation approach, and support evolving mid-play assignments rather than nearest-defender heuristics.

targets.the_leak: The API-Sports guide says API-NFL covers NFL and NCAA with quarter-by-quarter scores, historical games, standings, team/player statistics, injuries and bookmaker odds; its coverage flags should be checked because the injuries endpoint returns only currently injured players and does not preserve injury history. It also documents a GET-only base URL and x-apisports-key authentication.
targets.action_item: Implement the documented GET endpoints and coverage.injuries check; store current injury snapshots separately because the endpoint does not retain injury history.
